From c8f62f73bbced3a79894655bdb0b625462d956fc Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Duoming Zhou <duoming@zju.edu.cn>
Date: Sat, 31 Jan 2026 10:47:31 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] wifi: mt76: mt7996: fix use-after-free bugs in
 mt7996_mac_dump_work()

When the mt7996 pci chip is detaching, the mt7996_crash_data is
released in mt7996_coredump_unregister(). However, the work item
dump_work may still be running or pending, leading to UAF bugs
when the already freed crash_data is dereferenced again in
mt7996_mac_dump_work().

The race condition can occur as follows:

CPU 0 (removal path)               | CPU 1 (workqueue)
mt7996_pci_remove()                | mt7996_sys_recovery_set()
 mt7996_unregister_device()        |  mt7996_reset()
  mt7996_coredump_unregister()     |   queue_work()
   vfree(dev->coredump.crash_data) | mt7996_mac_dump_work()
                                   |  crash_data-> // UAF

Fix this by ensuring dump_work is properly canceled before
the crash_data is deallocated. Add cancel_work_sync() in
mt7996_unregister_device() to synchronize with any pending
or executing dump work.

Fixes: 878161d5d4a4 ("wifi: mt76: mt7996: enable coredump support")
Signed-off-by: Duoming Zhou <duoming@zju.edu.cn>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260131024731.18741-1-duoming@zju.edu.cn
Signed-off-by: Felix Fietkau <nbd@nbd.name>

diff --git a/drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/mt7996/init.c b/drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/mt7996/init.c
index 3b4f808b968c..29bce7cffbb5 100644
--- a/drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/mt7996/init.c
+++ b/drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/mt7996/init.c
@@ -1773,6 +1773,7 @@ int mt7996_register_device(struct mt7996_dev *dev)
 
 void mt7996_unregister_device(struct mt7996_dev *dev)
 {
+	cancel_work_sync(&dev->dump_work);
 	cancel_work_sync(&dev->wed_rro.work);
 	mt7996_unregister_phy(mt7996_phy3(dev));
 	mt7996_unregister_phy(mt7996_phy2(dev));
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File: `drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/mt7996/init.c`

- **Added** a call to `cancel_work_sync(&dev->dump_work)` at the beginning of the `mt7996_unregister_device()` function, before any other cleanup operations.

### Relationship Between Modifications

The bug was a use-after-free (UAF) caused by a race condition during device removal. The `dump_work` work item (`mt7996_mac_dump_work()`) could still be running or pending after the `crash_data` was freed by `mt7996_coredump_unregister()`. The fix ensures that the dump work is fully canceled **before** any release of the `crash_data` occurs (which happens later in the removal path), thus preventing the UAF. The modification is a single, targeted synchronization point that serializes the work item cancellation with the removal sequence.

Here is the commit message:
wifi: mt76: mt7996: fix use-after-free bugs in
 mt7996_mac_dump_work()

When the mt7996 pci chip is detaching, the mt7996_crash_data is
released in mt7996_coredump_unregister(). However, the work item
dump_work may still be running or pending, leading to UAF bugs
when the already freed crash_data is dereferenced again in
mt7996_mac_dump_work().

The race condition can occur as follows:

CPU 0 (removal path)               | CPU 1 (workqueue)
mt7996_pci_remove()                | mt7996_sys_recovery_set()
 mt7996_unregister_device()        |  mt7996_reset()
  mt7996_coredump_unregister()     |   queue_work()
   vfree(dev->coredump.crash_data) | mt7996_mac_dump_work()
                                   |  crash_data-> // UAF

Fix this by ensuring dump_work is properly canceled before
the crash_data is deallocated. Add cancel_work_sync() in
mt7996_unregister_device() to synchronize with any pending
or executing dump work.

Fixes: 878161d5d4a4 ("wifi: mt76: mt7996: enable coredump support")
Signed-off-by: Duoming Zhou <duoming@zju.edu.cn>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260131024731.18741-1-duoming@zju.edu.cn
Signed-off-by: Felix Fietkau <nbd@nbd.name>

Here is the root cause:
The bug is a use-after-free race condition during device removal. The work item `dump_work` (handled by `mt7996_mac_dump_work()`) can still be running or pending when `mt7996_coredump_unregister()` frees the `crash_data` pointer. The removal path in `mt7996_unregister_device()` did not cancel the dump work before deallocating the data, allowing a concurrent workqueue execution to access already freed memory.

Here is the patch:
 
 void mt7996_unregister_device(struct mt7996_dev *dev)
 {
+	cancel_work_sync(&dev->dump_work);
 	cancel_work_sync(&dev->wed_rro.work);
 	mt7996_unregister_phy(mt7996_phy3(dev));
 	mt7996_unregister_phy(mt7996_phy2(dev));
 	mt7996_unregister_thermal(&dev->phy);
 	mt7996_coredump_unregister(dev);
 	mt76_unregister_device(&dev->mt76);
 	mt7996_wed_rro_free(dev);
 	mt7996_mcu_exit(dev);
 	mt7996_tx_token_put(dev);
 	mt7996_dma_cleanup(dev);
 	if (mt7996_has_hwrro(dev) &&
 	    !mtk_wed_device_active(&dev->mt76.mmio.wed))
 		mt7996_rro_msdu_page_map_free(dev);
 	tasklet_disable(&dev->mt76.irq_tasklet);
 
 	mt76_free_device(&dev->mt76);
 }
--
